title: Investigate token-throughput asymmetry; hotfix rollout for Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted and Dedicated tenants) reported large TTFT variance and tokens/sec asymmetry between identical requests to the same model family. Impacted paths: small-context chat initiation and short-completion embedding calls. Symptoms: first-token latency increased from ~80ms to 250-600ms for some tenants; sustained tokens/sec dropped by 30-60% under burst. Private deployments show the same behavior when running quantized variants.

Root cause hypothesis: recent kernel selection heuristic change (kernel-autoselect v2) mis-classifies certain quantized int8 kernels for medium-length prompts and multi-tenant prefetch traffic. That selection combined with aggressive KV-prefetch and per-router multiplexing resulted in head-of-line stalls and suboptimal vectorized kernels being chosen for the first tokens. Interplay with eviction: warmstart credits were being consumed unevenly leading to cold KV lookups particularly for Dedicated pools with heterogeneous model variants.

Immediate mitigation implemented: 1) Disable kernel-autoselect v2 on the serving side and force stable kernel path (runtime-1.23.4-hotfix flag). 2) Introduced a soft cap on per-tenant prefetch concurrency (default 3->1 for canary tenants). 3) Applied a temporary pin to existing KV cache policy to reduce eviction churn. These changes were rolled out as a controlled canary in Hosted (5% traffic) at 2026-03-13 21:00 UTC and to two Dedicated customer pools overnight. Private customers were informed with a reproducible patch and manual restart instructions.

Planned work / next steps: 
- Finalize kernel selection telemetry to capture decision vectors and correlating context-length and quantization metadata (ETA 48h).
- Add deterministic fallback: if first-token latency exceeds 200ms, immediately reroute to stable kernel for that request (runtime guard).
- Adjust prefetch heuristics to be workload-aware (short prompts vs long contexts) and add per-model prefetch profiles.
- Run a 30% hosted canary + one Dedicated region for 6 hours then full rollout if no regressions.
- Prepare a customer communication bundle and dashboards: per-tenant TTFT, tokens/sec, kernel path, KV miss-rate.

Links and artifacts: 
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/ttft-surge-debug 
- PR with hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4567 
- Postmortem doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-424860+TTFT+asymmetry+postmortem 
- Reproduction script: gs://redwood-eng/ttft/replicate.sh

Customer notes: 
- Kite Labs reported 3x support tickets when their ML endpoint experienced high TTFT during morning burst; logs attached in the support thread. 
- Peregrine Health (Dedicated) saw sustained tokens/sec drop impacting realtime inference SLA. Both customers were notified and given mitigations on 2026-03-13.
